ConocoPhillips rose 0.84% today to $136.12, recovering modestly from a sharp drop two days earlier when the stock fell nearly $5 on November 18th. The timing and magnitude of that selloff align closely with the collapse of climate negotiations at COP31, where governments rejected a draft deal that failed to address fossil fuels—a development that raised uncertainty about future regulatory and policy risks for oil majors.

The rebound today comes as oil prices have stabilized around $89–93 per barrel and amid ongoing Middle East tensions, with reports of Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries and new Iranian-backed strikes. These geopolitical flashpoints typically support energy stocks by creating supply concerns, which may be counterbalancing some of the policy headwinds the sector faced earlier in the week.
